summary: Step-by-step setup for WSL2 without systemd: quit Docker Desktop, shut down WSL, confirm systemd cgroup isn't registered, mount the systemd cgroup hierarchy as root, then start Docker Desktop. Must be redone after all WSL instances stop.
questions: How do I mount the systemd cgroup in WSL2 for ansible-test?
Why does ansible-test --docker fail on WSL2?
Do I need to redo the WSL2 cgroup setup after wsl --shutdown?
How do I check if systemd cgroup exists in WSL?

answer_card.title: Prepare WSL2 for ansible-test --docker
answer_card.answer_md:
Redo this whenever all WSL instances have stopped.
1. Quit Docker Desktop (taskbar icon > Quit).
2. `wsl --shutdown`, then confirm with `wsl -l -v`.
3. In a WSL instance, as root, check `grep systemd /proc/self/cgroup` returns nothing (if it matches, recheck the Docker settings).
4. Mount the hierarchy:
   ```shell
   mkdir /sys/fs/cgroup/systemd
   mount cgroup -t cgroup /sys/fs/cgroup/systemd -o none,name=systemd,xattr
   ```
5. Start Docker Desktop. `--docker` should now work.
